Unexpected Visit.outcome: Tutorial with no lasting branches. Joining the dung prank earns a scolding from Martin but nothing worse; skipping it costs only some early friendship flavour.
Unexpected Visit.tip: Mother's opening questions set starting stats. Answer 'They are not drunks', then 'Give me an example' to unlock Martin's Kuttenberg talk. Buy the ale last – it warms.
Unexpected Visit.immersion: Let Henry be a lazy, cocky village lad here: sleep-heavy, eager for fights and pranks. Don't strip the house or steal the charcoal; that's not yet who he is.

Run!.outcome: Whistling to scare the Cumans off Theresa changes her later dialogue for the better. Asking Lady Stephanie for help is the cleanest escape; pleading with Robard costs reputation.
Run!.tip: Ride without stopping – the arrow wound kills you if you dawdle. Leaving Talmberg: Stephanie points you to a guard disguise, then talk Radim into opening the gate.
Run!.immersion: Never draw on the Cumans. At Talmberg, take only the guard kit you need for the disguise rather than raiding every chest a frightened refugee wouldn't touch.

Homecoming.outcome: Story-driven; the graveside fight plays out the same regardless. Sparing the road looters costs nothing – and the second one counts as a civilian murder if killed.
Homecoming.tip: The looters crumble after a hit or two and surrender; sheathe your sword when they yield. Draw on Zbyshek and he bolts, leaving the spade.
Homecoming.immersion: Walk, don't sprint, through Rovna and Skalitz and pause at the bodies. Bianca's ring is only available now – keeping it as a keepsake suits Henry; looting strangers doesn't.

Ordinary Routine.outcome: Finishing every morning chore earns Father's full coin and pocket money; botching them costs reputation and cash. Confirming the dance at the end fails anything unfinished.
Ordinary Routine.tip: Do the chickens, Tinker and the weeding before speaking to Father. Wrap up Cry Wolf! and Matchmaker before agreeing to go to the dance.
Ordinary Routine.immersion: Play Theresa as a busy miller's daughter: chat with neighbours, don't loot the town. Tell Henry the beer is from you – a small, in-character nudge that also earns reputation.

Cry Wolf!.outcome: Give the magpie's ring to Bianca to keep her goodwill; keeping it boosts Theresa's charisma but sours Bianca. The wolf must be shot either way.
Cry Wolf!.tip: Borrow Adam's bow (with 20 arrows) by promising him a dance. When Bianca starts picking, face west – the wolf comes from that side.
Cry Wolf!.immersion: Killing a wolf is fine under the no-kills rule; it's an animal threatening a friend. Keep close to Bianca rather than wandering off to explore.

Matchmaker.outcome: Telling Matthias that Johanka likes him pleases everyone. Just stealing the dice completes it but leaves Matthias sore; you can still pocket the lucky die for farkle.
Matchmaker.tip: Ask Fritz about lockpicking – it's the easy way to get Theresa some lockpicks before the day's events.
Matchmaker.immersion: A friend's favour, not a heist: talk first, and only lift the die if Johanka's plan needs it.

The Family Silver.outcome: Story-driven DLC errand with no meaningful branches; completing it is required to finish Ordinary Routine.
The Family Silver.tip: Finish the optional Skalitz errands first; once this is done, the evening dance is the next step and agreeing to it fails anything left over.
The Family Silver.immersion: Theresa is covering for her family, not getting rich: take only what the task needs and keep it quiet around Janek and Jaroslav.

Unexpected Visit (Theresa).outcome: Story-driven; the raid and its outcome are fixed. Doing the optional chores only adds flavour.
Unexpected Visit (Theresa).tip: The trunk by the stove has a bandage for battered Zbyshek. Stop at the tavern – Bianca hands over a Saviour Schnapps before things go wrong.
Unexpected Visit (Theresa).immersion: Do the morning chores properly; it's Theresa's last ordinary morning and the contrast with what follows is the point.

Thicker than Water.outcome: Story-driven. There's no knockout option for the Cuman in the mill; sneaking past him through the window is the only way to keep the no-kills rule.
Thicker than Water.tip: Crouch, leave the looting Cuman alone and slip out through the window into the barn. A Saviour Schnapps sits in the wheelbarrow outside the collapsed southern shaft.
Thicker than Water.immersion: Theresa is fleeing, not fighting: hug the palisade, use the dark and keep Tinker close. No looting bodies for gear she can't use anyway.

Ties that Bind.outcome: The ending is fixed – nothing you do changes it, so don't reload to try. Scaring off the looter at the crashed wagon keeps the no-kills rule.
Ties that Bind.tip: Water is right at the first junction inside the mine. The crashed wagon east has five marigolds and linen; pick the rest north on the east side of the road.
Ties that Bind.immersion: Do it at night as the game sets it; move between cover. Franta's plea for mercy is optional – refusing fits a Theresa who isn't a killer.

Aftermath.outcome: Story-driven ending to Theresa's flashback; its key events can't be avoided. Rescuing every survivor along the way (Angel of Mercy) is the only real variable.
Aftermath.tip: Rescue everyone in Angel of Mercy before going through Skalitz's north-east gate – that's where the finale begins.
Aftermath.immersion: Pause at the mill on the way; Theresa sees her family there. Walk the ruins rather than sprinting through.

Angel of Mercy.outcome: Saving all five survivors (Holba, Stanislav, Jarmila, Julian, Marosh) earns the Saviour achievement. Lying to Stanislav's looter avoids a fight; handing over the coin works too.
Angel of Mercy.tip: Holba needs two bandages. Julian's axe is on a stump under the lean-to; Stanislav's keys lie by the spilled wood basket, his purse in the pantry's apple basket.
Angel of Mercy.immersion: Tell Marosh the truth about Pavlena rather than leaving him searching; that's Theresa's whole character here.

The Good Thief.outcome: Paying 100 groschen settles it honestly; the ring job opens the millers' fencing network and thief work. Once you've taken the job, paying as well gains nothing.
The Good Thief.tip: Digging the grave finds nothing – the ring is in an easy chest in Hermann's bedroom. Tell him Peshek owes him flour and he'll hurry off.
The Good Thief.immersion: Henry should resent this: do it once he's broke, at night, in dark clothes. Bring raw meat for Hermann's dogs rather than hurting them.

Rob the Rich, Give to the Poor.outcome: The Vagabond ends up in the stocks, so the final seal can't be handed in for pay – sell it to a miller. Earlier jobs split the coin.
Rob the Rich, Give to the Poor.tip: Needs Pickpocketing first. Rob the rich woman while she sews with her back to the door.
Rob the Rich, Give to the Poor.immersion: For the first two jobs you may pay the 50 groschen yourself instead of stealing – ideal if Henry still doubts the Vagabond's story.

Do Me a Favour - Punch Me!.outcome: Beating all three unlocks repeat bouts – small wagers but excellent early strength, agility, unarmed and defence XP.
Do Me a Favour - Punch Me!.tip: Wear a gambeson and helmet – the brawlers ignore armour, so you take little damage. Fight Milan aggressively to drain his stamina, then clinch.
Do Me a Favour - Punch Me!.immersion: Fists only, fair play: don't loot your knocked-out opponents, even though the game lets you. Treat it as refugee lads letting off steam.

Scavenger.outcome: Returning cup and coin to Beran earns a small reward – the honest end. Kunesh can't pay either way; finish this to recruit him for Pribyslavitz later.
Scavenger.tip: Skalitz always spawns a skirmish – wait it out, or go while Fritz and Matthew are walking to Ledetchko, when skirmishes are disabled. The other dove-cote holds only rags.
Scavenger.immersion: Going back to Skalitz is personal – ride in by day, pause at home, and don't treat the town as a loot run.

Chumps on the River.outcome: Win to triple your stake; second place returns it. Landing 16 or more hits once earns bow training from Vatzek.
Chumps on the River.tip: Use a light, fast bow, or ride across at the crossing and shoot from the far bank, nearer the logs. Leaving the area or getting hit forfeits the bet.

A Man of the Cloth.outcome: Fetching Father Simon settles him in Rovna and makes In God's Hands easier. Father Francis pays the same but stays in Sasau. Both give 250 groschen.
A Man of the Cloth.tip: Talk the tramps into freeing Simon – the creek terrain is poor for fighting. Then leave the area at once, or Simon may walk into the bandit camp and die.
A Man of the Cloth.immersion: Visit Mary's parents rather than relying on markers, and follow the comfrey along the creek; Henry tracks him like a local would.

Pickpocketing.outcome: Simple training; Peshek always takes his dagger back. Repeatable whenever you want practice.
Pickpocketing.tip: Crouch directly behind him and release before the circle turns red. If he wanders off, just talk to him to restart.
Pickpocketing.immersion: Henry learns this reluctantly; it's a skill for later, not a habit. Avoid practising on random townsfolk afterwards.

Thick as Thieves - Peshek.outcome: Pays roughly 150, 175 and 250 groschen. Hanush's book is the riskiest theft in the game early on; getting caught in the upper castle hurts reputation badly.
Thick as Thieves - Peshek.tip: Rob the bathhouse chest by day while upstairs is empty. The deed is on a table in the bailiff's private chamber behind a Hard door; drink Padfoot first.
Thick as Thieves - Peshek.immersion: Stealing from Hanush, Henry's own patron, is a big line – do it at night in dark clothes, and only once Henry has reasons to resent the town.

Thick as Thieves - Woyzeck.outcome: Pays around 250 for the waffenrocks and 300 for the horse. Must be finished before the attack on Vranik in The Die is Cast, or it becomes impossible.
Thick as Thieves - Woyzeck.tip: Stephanie's chest is Very Hard: Lockpicking 15, or 10 with Padfoot. Any Merhojed horse counts. The armoury key can be taken from a sleeping guard in the left tower.
Thick as Thieves - Woyzeck.immersion: Stephanie once helped Henry – robbing her is a betrayal. Go at night in dark, quiet clothes and keep it out of Henry's later conversations with her.

A Woman Scorned.outcome: Completing it leads to the farmer and his wife being murdered, and the old whore vanishes. Henry was used; there's no good ending.
A Woman Scorned.tip: Ask Andrew at the inn after 2pm the next day to learn the outcome. Afterwards the farmhouse works as a free bed and stash in Neuhof.
A Woman Scorned.immersion: Henry doesn't know what he's enabling, so play it straight – then let the news land; avoid bed-sleeping in the dead couple's house if that jars.

The Horse That Bolted.outcome: Bringing Pie back unharmed pays groschen plus a free horse caparison. If Pie is hurt, the groom attacks you with a scythe.
The Horse That Bolted.tip: Thistle asks 500 groschen – beat him in a fistfight or talk him round instead. Follow the dung and ask locals. Park Pie carefully: you can't remount him.
The Horse That Bolted.immersion: Track Pie on foot or at a walk, asking locals as you go; skip the markers. Henry knows horses from Skalitz.

Mightier than the Sword.outcome: Unlocks reading – needed for Last Will and Testament and Honeyed Words, helps Pestilence, and opens skill books and alchemy recipes.
Mightier than the Sword.tip: Do it early: 50 groschen and no in-game days pass. Afterwards, flick through lore books cover to cover for quick reading XP.
Mightier than the Sword.immersion: A blacksmith's son who couldn't read is exactly Henry. Read in the evenings at an inn rather than mid-road.

Restless Spirit.outcome: Long, multi-day chain ending in Drahomira's confession; telling her to come clean or keep quiet is flavour. Rewards include 375 groschen and her ring.
Restless Spirit.tip: Monks sleep at 11pm. Take only the Necronomicon – leave the torn page (needed for Scattered Pages). The marker wrongly points to Rattay. Meet the Apothecary at 21:00.
Restless Spirit.immersion: Henry is superstitious enough to try the rituals in earnest. Go to graves at dusk and keep to the schedule; don't skip-time through the whole thing.

Tricks of the Trade.outcome: Either way you get 100 groschen. Asking Mikesh openly works; there's no penalty for honesty.
Tricks of the Trade.tip: Write the ditty down as he sings it. Mentioning Martin as a blacksmith may win you the full explanation of the tempering secret.
Tricks of the Trade.immersion: This is Henry's trade – ask Mikesh as one smith's son to another rather than spying.

Thick as Thieves - Simon.outcome: Pays about 175, 225 and 250 groschen. The cobbler may be punished over the lost spurs.
Thick as Thieves - Simon.tip: Take the brocade at night – it's folded on a shelf in the tailor's workshop. The beer recipe sits on a shelf in the room with Henry's Uzhitz inn bed.
Thick as Thieves - Simon.immersion: Steal the recipe while renting that very room, so Henry has a reason to be there. Avoid carrying the stolen spurs past Sasau guards.

The Queen of Sheba's Sword.outcome: Reward is the chance to buy the reforged sword (around 1,600 groschen). Don't kill Zach in Sasau – he's needed in later quests.
The Queen of Sheba's Sword.tip: Bring lockpicks and 200 groschen. The Rattay blacksmith's piece is on a storeroom shelf even before Aquarius; Ledetchko's smith simply sells his.
The Queen of Sheba's Sword.immersion: Buy where you can and pickpocket where you must; avoid knocking Zach out in front of his son.

Fat Profits.outcome: Each delivery raises the butcher's opinion but costs a little reputation with the monastery. The final order needs 60 boar, 140 red deer and 150 hare at once.
Fat Profits.tip: Take the Butcher perk first for offal and liver. One big hunt east of Talmberg with a strong-packed horse covers the final order.
Fat Profits.immersion: It's poaching: hunt in the early morning away from roads, and don't sell game openly in Sasau the same day.

A Friend In Need....outcome: Getting them hired at Ledetchko mill helps old friends and sets up later repayment. Miller Oliver can be convinced, threatened or bribed – convincing is kindest.
A Friend In Need....tip: Pick 'They're basically my neighbours' with Oliver for reputation. While the lads walk to Ledetchko, random skirmishes are off – handy for risky trips like Skalitz.
A Friend In Need....immersion: Henry should be glad to see them alive. Tell Theresa they survived; check back after a week rather than chasing the money.

Green-Eyed Monster.outcome: The jobs escalate towards framing and arson; the farmhand is later said to have been caught and hanged. The rewards are modest.
Green-Eyed Monster.tip: Lift the draper's tinderbox from him at night while he sleeps; his wife and shop guard are around by day.
Green-Eyed Monster.immersion: Henry can see where this leads by the third job. If you play him strictly, stop after the amulet, which recovers wages actually owed.

A Costly Brawl.outcome: Persuading Brother Elias wipes the 100-groschen debt for free; paying it yourself works but costs coin.
A Costly Brawl.tip: Elias has low Speech and intimidation stats, so either option works without prep. Don't push Fritz too hard – he'll throw a punch.
A Costly Brawl.immersion: Ask Johanka about the brawl first; she gives the real story, and it lets Henry argue from fact.

In God's Hands.outcome: Helping every patient saves them and earns rewards, including Semek's vitality secret. Delay and Hannes dies around day three or four.
In God's Hands.tip: Find Father Simon first. Bring ten bandages, Lullaby ingredients, comfrey and Artemisia, plus ~150 groschen for the Custodian. His later speech check can be buggy and lead to jail.
In God's Hands.immersion: Stay at the monastery until it's done – no side trips. Repeat lullabies for the insomniac; it's patient care, and he eventually teaches alchemy.

Saintly Remains.outcome: The real bowl from Procopius's cave needs no Speech check; fake bones do. Reward is identical either way. Keep the bowl and Urban later picks a fight.
Saintly Remains.tip: Easiest way in: the side hallway off the church nave (by the indulgence box), through the door and down the ladder—no lock, no guards.
Saintly Remains.immersion: Honest Henry brings the genuine bowl, not a grave-robbed bone or the Charlatan's fake, and puts it back in the cave afterwards.

Weeds.outcome: Pull only dandelions, nettles and thistles for 75 groschen and Nicodemus's goodwill; uproot too much mint, eyebright or comfrey and he pays nothing.
Weeds.tip: Comfrey bed needs weeding too. High Herbalism picks fast, so check the prompt names a weed before pressing—one slip grabs a medicinal herb.
Weeds.immersion: Henry is a novice under obedience: do it in daylight as part of the monastery's work, not at night.

New Herbarium.outcome: No choices—deliver one of each of fifteen herbs plus an old book.
New Herbarium.tip: Fresh from Weeds you already hold nettle, dandelion and thistle. Sage, St John's wort and marigold grow just outside the walls; comfrey is in his garden.
New Herbarium.immersion: Gather specimens yourself in the fields rather than lifting them off Nicodemus's own shelf by his alchemy bench.

Tough Love.outcome: Telling the truth about the cold in-laws and revealing Hermann's love lets Elishka stay happily (200 groschen). Sending her away pays 125 and leaves her miserable.
Tough Love.tip: Carry an Embrocation for the scribe. Bribing the mother-in-law is the surest way through her. Talk to Hermann again afterwards—the reward isn't automatic.
Tough Love.immersion: Never take the hidden option of killing the in-laws; Henry settles this with words.

...Is a Friend Indeed.outcome: The ambush pays 175 and keeps the lads in work. Stealing Martin's scarf and handing it to Jane exposes Thomas properly. Killing Thomas fails the quest.
...Is a Friend Indeed.tip: Timed—fails within a few days. When luring Thomas, correct him that Peshek is from Rattay and drop 'The Wren', or he smells a rat.
...Is a Friend Indeed.immersion: Fists only. Henry is helping friends teach a bully a lesson, not committing murder in Ledetchko.

Skin.outcome: 70 groschen per batch, 210 in total. Brada's promised hunting lesson appears bugged and gives nothing.
Skin.tip: Pick it up before becoming Divish's master huntsman in Cherchez la Femme; afterwards it can't be started. Not every hare yields a pelt.
Skin.immersion: It's poaching on Divish's land: hunt at dawn or dusk in quiet clothes, well away from roads and Talmberg's guards.

The House of God.outcome: Stopping Zmola clears the Talmberg quarry's name, but since patch 1.9.1 Divish pays nothing. When the stone drops, run straight to the mill—going via the Overseer gets Leshek killed.
The House of God.tip: Timed once clues are gathered. Bring a blunt weapon for the mason on the scaffolding. The 'Fallen block' may stay in your inventory—weightless, harmless.
The House of God.immersion: Henry acts as Divish's investigator: ride the Talmberg–Sasau road, question everyone, and keep the night meeting at the scaffolding as agreed.

Masquerade.outcome: Real raven feathers, wolf fangs and a dog killed at night earn the Magical Cuman disguise; substitutes give the plain one. Same stats either way.
Masquerade.tip: Only face-plated Cuman helmets count; repair damaged armour before Andrew accepts it. Bane in the camp stew at night is the safest raid.
Masquerade.immersion: Henry agrees out of grief, not greed: rob only Cumans, and do the dog hunt by moonlight as the superstition demands.

Besmirched.outcome: Returning everything, cross included, to Adam is the honourable ending; Andrew pays 575 instead. The cross also secures Adam for Pribyslavitz's tavern.
Besmirched.tip: Get Tonchek's name from Andrew with Speech, inspect the new kettle by his hut, and find his stash in a rotting tree just north. Andrew sells the cross for 150.
Besmirched.immersion: Adam is Bianca's brother and a Skalitz neighbour: hand it all back and refuse his money.

Lost in Translation.outcome: Stash holds 800 groschen, an antidote and two Saviour Schnapps; the bailiff adds 100 for the live Cuman. Killing him yourself fails the quest.
Lost in Translation.tip: Ask the Vagrant whether he translated everything—pass the check and you dodge the Cuman's ambush. Travel with the Vagrant; alone he often gets lost.
Lost in Translation.immersion: Walk the prisoner to Rattay without fast travel and keep him close, or he bolts. Honest Henry pays the Miller his share.

Awakening.outcome: Story-driven, no choices. Not timed—you can explore before reporting to Radzig.
Awakening.tip: Fight the Cumans in the fever dream for a little XP. Bow training with Berthold stays locked until after Train Hard, Fight Easy.
Awakening.immersion: Henry's whole aim is Radzig and the sword—head up to Pirkstein once the debt is in hand, not after weeks of wandering.

Train Hard, Fight Easy.outcome: Beat Hans at both archery and the duel to win his hunting bow; one win each means no exchange; lose both and he takes 2 groschen.
Train Hard, Fight Easy.tip: Archery: finish first for three bonus points and loose as soon as fully drawn. Duel: aim for Hans's bare head. Afterwards Bernard offers further training—take it.
Train Hard, Fight Easy.immersion: Show up in your own modest clothes; a blacksmith's son in stolen finery undercuts the scene with Hans.

Rattay Tourney.outcome: Each win pays 400 groschen and a prize; the first five complete the Lords of Leipa armour. Losing costs only the entry fee.
Rattay Tourney.tip: Drink potions before speaking to the herald—there's no break and your inventory is locked. Any crime in Rattay gets you banned. Enrol before 15:00.
Rattay Tourney.immersion: Fight fairly under Radzig's name; skip the trick of knocking out rivals the night before.

Who Do You Like.outcome: A win returns five times your stake, despite Peshek saying double. Lose, or skip the tourney, and the stake is gone. He stops taking bets after about five.
Who Do You Like.tip: The bet only covers the next tourney, so wager when you're ready to fight that day.
Who Do You Like.immersion: Peshek nursed Henry back to health; a modest wager suits Henry better than draining the old man.

Dead Men Tell No Tales.outcome: Win, beat Black Peter in his ambush and bring his poisoned sword: 85 groschen and the best Samopesh reputation. Sparing or fleeing him pays 70.
Dead Men Tell No Tales.tip: Ride from Rattay towards Samopesh past Peshek's mill—don't fast-travel or the rope-trap ambush won't trigger. Carry an antidote; his blade is poisoned.
Dead Men Tell No Tales.immersion: Hear the Samopesh blacksmith's story before your first tourney win, or his dialogue won't make sense.

Money for Old Rope.outcome: Sabotage all three for 400 groschen, three books (Bane and Lazarus recipes) and the Spoilsport achievement. Killing Heinz voids the reward; betraying Hermann fails it.
Money for Old Rope.tip: Bring poison, poisoned meat for the dog and the rotten rope. Henry must be able to read. Dull the sword on Rattay's smithy grindstone, then return it before dawn.
Money for Old Rope.immersion: Hermann forbids murder—knock people out, never kill—and watch the 2 p.m. executions from the crowd.

A Bird in the Hand....outcome: 150 groschen, 40 arrows and a big jump in Berthold's reputation, which means cheaper arrows.
A Bird in the Hand....tip: Drop a trap where the song is loudest and wait an hour. A bandit camp sits beside the second bird. Pick belladonna while you wait.
A Bird in the Hand....immersion: Go on foot by day without noisy armour, actually listening for the birds rather than following the map marker.

Keeping the Peace.outcome: Story-driven. Settle Beggar Jane's dispute with Speech or Charisma; intimidating the armoursmith always fails. The tavern brawl with Hans can't be won.
Keeping the Peace.tip: Wear at least a gambeson and helmet or Nightingale scolds you. While on the watch, guards don't search you for stolen goods.
Keeping the Peace.immersion: Carry a torch after dark as ordered, and give Jane alms yourself—the blacksmith's son knows charity.

Courtship.outcome: Committing after the third date (A Woman's Lot) unlocks further dates, the Smitten buff, clothing repairs and gifts. Refusing breaks her heart for good.
Courtship.tip: First date 07:00–12:00, second 16:00–20:00. Avoid the evening date the night before a tourney you've bet on—it can fail the tourney.
Courtship.immersion: Stay faithful: skip bathhouse extras and the Alpha Male perk, which makes Theresa suspect cheating. Wash and wear clean clothes before calling.

The Prey.outcome: Shoot one hare to win 100 groschen. Rescuing Hans earns Radzig's service and Pebbles.
The Prey.tip: Arrive mounted and Hans is merely dazed—straight fight. On foot you can return at night and take the sleeping Cumans quietly. Keep clear of Hans while hunting or lose 15.
The Prey.immersion: Wear quiet hunting clothes, and cook hares only after Hans has counted them.

The Hunt Begins.outcome: Riding out at once lets you overhear the bandits naming Ginger—extra dialogue later. Vanishing for over a day angers Bernard.
The Hunt Begins.tip: You must mount Pebbles even if you own a horse. Badassness always works on Mark. Search both bandits for the hoof-pick.
The Hunt Begins.immersion: Report each finding to Bernard before moving on—Henry is under his command now.

Ginger in a Pickle.outcome: Clear the bandits hunting Ginger and convince Zora: he returns home, later pays 150 plus Horsemanship XP, and you earn the 'Ginger' achievement.
Ginger in a Pickle.tip: Get Bernard's leave first. At the Talmberg charcoal-burners, follow the twin who slips away—he leads straight to Ginger. Bernard will help with the bandits if asked.
Ginger in a Pickle.immersion: Don't lie to Zora about 'no loose ends'—kill the bandits first so Henry's promise to Ginger is true.

Mysterious Ways.outcome: Win Godwin's trust and preach well and he names the gang; fail and you need the Rattay scribe and an Embrocation instead.
Mysterious Ways.tip: Sermon: open confidently, then answer harshly twice; pick 'God stands at the head', 'To sin is human' and defend Godwin. Never draw steel in the tavern brawl.
Mysterious Ways.immersion: Search Lubosh's house properly first, and dress again after the binge before you preach.

On the Scent.outcome: Reach Reeky in time to hear the full story, then free him, kill him or take him to Rattay for trial. Arrive late and he dies.
On the Scent.tip: Talk to the tanner first, then Adela—that order unlocks Raspberry's directions to the cave. Two bandits drink in the Ledetchko inn until 18:00; don't attack them in town.
On the Scent.immersion: Handing Reeky over for trial is the lawful choice for one of Radzig's men.

My Friend Timmy.outcome: Telling Morcock earns 450 groschen and the camp's location; letting his men kill Timmy keeps Mirka recruitable, unlike killing him yourself.
My Friend Timmy.tip: Never walk into Pribyslavitz with Morcock—his chief orders you killed. Report to Radzig first and use Morcock's name only to scout.
My Friend Timmy.immersion: Don't follow to watch Timmy die; meet Morcock at the Samopesh inn and keep your hands clean.

Nest of Vipers.outcome: Poison all four pots and burn all four arrow caches to weaken the battle. Answer 'There's quite a few'—asking for every soldier gets Kolben's farm burned.
Nest of Vipers.tip: Bring a torch and poisons (five spares lie around camp). The stable north of the Cuman side has a free disguise. Burning arrows alerts anyone nearby—do it last.
Nest of Vipers.immersion: This is reconnaissance for Radzig: scout at night in Cuman gear and don't sit down for drinks with Morcock.

Baptism of Fire.outcome: Story-driven, no choices; earlier sabotage decides how hard it gets.
Baptism of Fire.tip: Learn master strikes before Runt; bring several Aqua Vitalis and Buck's Blood. Burn the haystack before the Cuman gate to flush the archers. Don't skip the post-duel cutscene.
Baptism of Fire.immersion: Fight alongside Radzig's men in proper armour—no sneaking off. This is Henry's revenge; let it feel earned.

Ruin.outcome: 100 groschen per leader's spurs and 35 per ear across four camps; finishing unlocks Raiders.
Ruin.tip: Kill the leader first. Bane in the pot or wineskin at night clears a camp safely. A horse in camp can be spooked to draw bandits away.
Ruin.immersion: Henry finds ear-cutting barbaric—taking just the spurs still completes it.

Aquarius.outcome: Best: water—Tonda, Pickman, Vincent; latrines—Rock and Antonia; Kornelius unemployed for later. Vincent on latrines kills himself; Antonia on water loses her husband.
Aquarius.tip: Have a marigold decoction at the interview—Rock can't be helped afterwards. Visit Father Francis in Sasau rather than lying to Agnes.
Aquarius.immersion: Honour Theresa's plea for Antonia and Vincent; Henry looks after his Skalitz neighbours.

Beggars' Feast.outcome: Small payments per delivery, but each hand-in costs reputation with Rattay's citizens and soldiers—it's poaching.
Beggars' Feast.tip: Hares are everywhere; boar south of Rattay; roe and red deer to the east. Hand meat in raw before it spoils.
Beggars' Feast.immersion: Hunt quietly at dusk and carry the meat to Alex discreetly—Henry is breaking Hanush's law to feed his people.

Waldensians.outcome: If the Bauers flee, the Vicar pays nothing but Hanush gives 225 and St Michael's sword—unless you admit warning them. Killing the Vicar earns nothing.
Waldensians.tip: Some arguments with Mistress Bauer need about 15+ Speech; bring a Bard potion. Timed—dawdle and the Vicar finishes the job himself.
Waldensians.immersion: Never hand the Bauers to the Vicar; spilling a churchman's blood should be Henry's very last resort.

Fishy Business in Uzhitz.outcome: Beat all four for small purses and the Agile as a Weasel I book. Repeatable for unarmed practice.
Fishy Business in Uzhitz.tip: Fight Josef, Maple and Mash in that order, then the fisherman. Bets are 5 and 10 groschen; go in rested and fed.
Fishy Business in Uzhitz.immersion: Honest bare-knuckle sport between quests suits Henry well.

Playing with the Devil.outcome: Someone dies whatever you do; saving the women means killing two 'devils'. Godwin and Gertrude reproach you regardless. Interfering forfeits the Virgin achievement.
Playing with the Devil.tip: Strip noisy gear; the women meet at the crossroads west of Uzhitz around 21:00. If they spot you, they try again the next night.
Playing with the Devil.immersion: Go on foot after dark and report truthfully to Godwin and Gertrude.

Raiders.outcome: 375 groschen per leader's faceplate and 35 per ear across five camps; finishing unlocks Interlopers.
Raiders.tip: Cumans wear heavier armour than bandits—poison the pot or take sleepers with a dagger. The largest camp sometimes loses its leader underground; reload or wait for respawn.
Raiders.immersion: Henry is avenging Skalitz here; keep the faceplates as proof and leave plundering to what he'd actually use.

Hare Hunt.outcome: Mutually exclusive with Sheep in Wolf's Clothing — whichever you start first decides. Believing Hanekin leads to Cherchez la Femme either way.
Hare Hunt.tip: Ask Blacksmith's Betty what she saw before asking about poachers, or the clearing lead can vanish. Dig the bare patch east of the clearing's fire for the buried carcass.

Sheep in Wolf's Clothing.outcome: Siding with the poachers keeps Emergency Supply and Cherchez la Femme open, but locks out Hare Hunt for good. Siding with the guards costs Lukesh's trust and Emergency Supply.
Sheep in Wolf's Clothing.tip: Buy antlers from Huntsman Berthold or Konyash in Rattay rather than hunting a buck. Tell Nicholas about the horn plot and he hands it over. Save before the clearing.

Emergency Supply.outcome: Only offered if you sided with the poachers in Sheep in Wolf's Clothing. The stash is in the tankard by Lukesh's cooking pot; you have two days.
Emergency Supply.tip: If it somehow appears: the stash is in the tankard by Lukesh's cooking pot, and you have two days. Otherwise ignore the guide entry.

Cherchez la Femme.outcome: Believing Hare gets Nicholas's confession, the Talmberg hunting lodge, huntsman gear and his merchant chest. Killing Margaret, Hare or Nicholas fails it outright.
Cherchez la Femme.tip: Catch Margaret alone when she fetches water at the river and talk her into coming; no need to break in. Avoid letting the last stage clash with Rattay Tournament day.
Cherchez la Femme.immersion: Henry persuades rather than abducts by force; ask Hare's full story first so siding with him feels earned, not convenient.

Henry the Master Huntsman.outcome: Legal hunting around Talmberg plus 250 groschen per delivery. Turning the post down loses the lodge's purpose but nothing story-critical.
Henry the Master Huntsman.tip: Get the Butcher perk (Hunting 5) first. Hunt red deer and boar due east of the lodge; the requests are by weight, so big kills fill them fast.
Henry the Master Huntsman.immersion: Wear the green huntsman outfit and hazel bow from the lodge chest, hunt at dawn, and carry meat home on horseback rather than fast-travelling.

Delicacies.outcome: Andrew pays well for game, and as Master Huntsman Henry can legally tell gamekeepers to back off. The training reward is reportedly buggy.
Delicacies.tip: Hunt during Master Huntsman runs so one trip fills both orders: hares and boar north of the inn, roe deer in the woods towards Talmberg.
Delicacies.immersion: Frame it as repaying Andrew's tip, and hunt only what Talmberg can spare; a huntsman shouldn't strip his own woods for an innkeeper.

A Rock and a Hard Place.outcome: Both lads survive and the quest completes, so Matthew and Fritz can later work at Pribyslavitz (both must live). Letting the heist go ahead risks one or both dying.
A Rock and a Hard Place.tip: The wages sit in a hard chest in a Talmberg guard tower until they're moved; the quarry hut has a sleeping quarryman. Pick 'That makes sense' with Robard.
A Rock and a Hard Place.immersion: Henry argues against the robbery first; paying with his own coin keeps his hands clean and his friends alive. Never rob the quarrymen themselves.

Gallows Brothers.outcome: Leaving it open spares Andrew, Matthew and Fritz; reporting to Robard or framing anyone gets people hanged. It auto-fails at The Die is Cast.
Gallows Brothers.tip: Don't tell Matthew about Andrew's plan either; that opens the framing route. Killing Andrew also locks out Delicacies.
Gallows Brothers.immersion: Henry listens to Andrew out of courtesy but won't send friends to the gallows; just walk away from the dialogue.

The Sport of Kings.outcome: Winning earns 250 groschen and the best saddle, and Divish buys from Zora again. Second place pays 175 and only half the custom, not enough to save the stud.
The Sport of Kings.tip: Turn up at the Talmberg gate before noon on the grey; missing the start means no reward and a cold Divish.
The Sport of Kings.immersion: Ride the grey from Neuhof to Talmberg yourself, don't fast-travel; Henry is vouching for Zora's horse, so show it off on the road.

Talmberg Horse Race.outcome: A fair win settles The Sport of Kings properly. Pushing or shooting rivals out works but is cheap and can cost a fine.
Talmberg Horse Race.tip: Wear good spurs or drink Aesop. Hang back on the narrow Uzhitz path; after Merhojed, cut left and ford the shallows to the quarry, then climb straight to the castle.
Talmberg Horse Race.immersion: Race honestly on Zora's grey only; swapping to a faster horse undermines the point of proving Neuhof's stock.

At Your Service, My Lady.outcome: 125 groschen, Stephanie's shirt and a romance scene. Accepting her gift rules out the Virgin achievement; replacing the moldavite with a cheap stone shortchanges the crown.
At Your Service, My Lady.tip: Bring a bow for the Rattay archery contest. The moldavite is with two bandits by the river west of Sasau, past the blood-stained cart; easy lock.
At Your Service, My Lady.immersion: Tame the roan Vashek's way by singing to it, then ride it to Talmberg at walking pace; a wedding gift shouldn't arrive lathered.

Miracles While You Wait.outcome: A small reward and a lot of humour; the quest is about fake relics, so outcomes are mostly comic. Calming the crowd peacefully is the clean finish.
Miracles While You Wait.tip: Carry a bow for the topping-out branch and 150 groschen (or your favourite dice) for the gambler. Don't bid Mark goodbye; it can make him attack.
Miracles While You Wait.immersion: Henry sees through the charlatan; play it as amused curiosity, and fetch the tooth by coaxing Procopius to Mikesh rather than beating him.

Questions and Answers.outcome: Story-driven. Curing the bandit lets you question him properly, opening the better lead for All that Glisters; skipping the cure leaves only a letter from a corpse.
Questions and Answers.tip: Don't break into the barn early; cure Merhojed first. Radzig needs time to reach the Talmberg lookout, so finishing fast may mean waiting for him.
Questions and Answers.immersion: Ride to Merhojed rather than fast-travel, and check on Matthias first; Henry's friend lying hurt there matters more to him than the prisoner.

The King's Silver.outcome: Getting to the truth about the miners pays up to 900–1,200 groschen; whether to turn in the widow is your conscience. Very buggy quest.
The King's Silver.tip: Talk to Nemoy at the miners' camp before entering the shaft, or the quest can't finish. Bring a torch; return to the camp yourself afterwards, there's no prompt.
The King's Silver.immersion: Henry is from Skalitz; walk the ruined mineworks slowly and let the widow's plight weigh on the verdict rather than chasing the bounty.

Pestilence.outcome: A correct diagnosis saves all of Merhojed and the prisoner. A wrong cure or delay costs villagers' lives and the bandit's testimony.
Pestilence.tip: Talk to Matthias and every sick villager. Tell Nicodemus half are ill and all animals died: it's water poisoning (valerian, thistle, charcoal). Treat the bandit too.
Pestilence.immersion: Don't loot plague houses or sleep in Merhojed; dig Bedrishka's husband's grave before lifting him, as a neighbour would.

Last Will and Testament.outcome: Finding Elijah first sends him home to his dying father before the will is lodged. Delivering straight away pays 175 but disinherits him without a word.
Last Will and Testament.tip: Elijah sits outside the Tavern on the Green, usually by 17:00, and won't show in heavy rain. Speak to him before handing the will to Father Fabian.
Last Will and Testament.immersion: Henry writes the will as faithfully as he can; reconciling father and son is very much the boy Theresa would recognise.

Band of Bastards.outcome: Beating Dangler earns Kuno's respect and opens the DLC chain. Losing still progresses but leaves Henry at 1 health and bleeding.
Band of Bastards.tip: Dangler has no visor: stab at his face. Bring bandages anyway in case the duel goes badly.
Band of Bastards.immersion: Wear Radzig's colours or your best kit; Henry arrives as his lord's representative, there to keep sellswords in check, not to join them.

Lost in the Woods.outcome: Freeing Marius makes Henry Bailiff of Pribyslavitz. Claiming you paid a ransom gets 600 groschen from Divish even if you didn't, which Henry shouldn't do.
Lost in the Woods.tip: At night two bandits sleep and two sit by the fires; wait for them to split up and take them quietly. Don't say you want to join them.
Lost in the Woods.immersion: Finding Marius by chance while revisiting Pribyslavitz fits Henry best, since Divish never briefs him; then tell Divish the truth about the ransom.

Bad Blood.outcome: Linear: wipe out the raiders and report to Radzig. No meaningful choices, just your first taste of Kuno's band at work.
Bad Blood.tip: The clue is a note pinned to a shield in the north-east building of the burnt mill; if invisible, look for the dagger. Ask Stephan about the blood trail.
Bad Blood.immersion: Stay with the column on horseback rather than galloping ahead; Henry is the guide and should look the part.

The Ring of Bacchus.outcome: Rewards are books; the real value is camp banter. Keeping it unfinished until after What Price Honour? flags any of Kuno's men dying.
The Ring of Bacchus.tip: Stephan's ring is hidden in a nest; if it vanishes on landing it's a known bug. Pickpocket Jan instead of brawling, which costs reputation either way.
The Ring of Bacchus.immersion: Treat it as a camp game between battles: play it in the evenings at Kuno's fire, and don't sleep in camp while carrying the ring.

Uninvited Guests.outcome: Persuading Kuno to attack at once saves the women and earns Chivalrous Soul, but likely costs a man or two. Waiting is safer for the band.
Uninvited Guests.tip: Save before the speech check and the fight. Stick close to Kuno's men so enemies split their attention.
Uninvited Guests.immersion: Henry pushes to attack now; he has seen Skalitz burn and won't wait for drunk raiders to finish with the women.

A Tight Spot.outcome: A linear ambush escape. Survive and regroup — what you learn here drives the rest of the DLC.
A Tight Spot.tip: You don't need to kill everyone; the archers on the west bank stay put. Break out towards Kuno rather than chasing stragglers.
A Tight Spot.immersion: Ride out in daylight with the band and keep your horse close; no fast-travelling off before Kuno's debrief.

Thirty Pieces.outcome: Untying and freeing Jakey (Pinky Promise) later lets you remind Kuno of his oath. Killing him pleases Kuno; leaving him tied 12 hours earns Torturer.
Thirty Pieces.tip: If Jakey is invisible, talk to the tree he's tied to. Andrew may want a favour for the lead if Masquerade isn't done.
Thirty Pieces.immersion: Follow the trail of scarf, picnic and trousers on foot. Henry, who knows mercy, lets the frightened lad go once he talks.

What Price Honour?.outcome: Reminding Kuno of his promise (needs Jakey freed and Kuno warned) keeps him loyal. Silence lets him take Hagen's silver; bribing needs about 15,000 groschen.
What Price Honour?.tip: Don't loot Kuno's camp or his men fight barehanded. Fast-travel away straight after the battle so wounded men don't bleed out on the walk back.
What Price Honour?.immersion: Stand beside Kuno in Radzig's colours and speak for honour, not coin; buying a mercenary's loyalty doesn't suit Henry.

All that Glisters.outcome: Story-driven investigation with a few side choices (Ulrich, Rattled, Esther). Sparing Ulrich gives an ally for the workshop raid.
All that Glisters.tip: Show Borya the bloodstained bags behind his shed to force the truth. Catch Zach late at night to make him talk. Stash loot before confronting Rapota.
All that Glisters.immersion: Ride between Rovna, Rattay and Sasau rather than fast-travel, and dress modestly in Sasau; Henry is investigating quietly, like Feyfar in disguise.

Interlopers.outcome: 1,925 groschen per leader's spurs plus quality loot. The third camp, with four strong bandits and dogs, is the real danger.
Interlopers.tip: Poison the cooking pots or bring Bane-coated weapons and a dagger. Save before the third camp; collect spurs from each leader as proof.
Interlopers.immersion: Plan raids at night, approach on foot from the treeline, and travel between camps rather than teleporting.

Rattled.outcome: The bludgeon duel or stealing Ota's armour both pay the same; your side decides who moves to Pribyslavitz. Zach earns far more there than Ota.
Rattled.tip: Win the duel honestly; stealing the armour is easiest during the day when Ota's household stays downstairs.
Rattled.immersion: Fight the duel in the square rather than burgle Ota; an honest bout suits Henry far better than theft.

Damsel in Distress.outcome: Rescue Esther and Florian helps the investigation. A surrendering kidnapper can reveal an easier back entrance to the counterfeiters' workshop.
Damsel in Distress.tip: Loot the kidnappers' keys or you'll trigger a fetch in Rattay. Don't follow Esther home; she walks past skirmish spawns that can kill her.
Damsel in Distress.immersion: Go at night for a quiet rescue, or charge in armour; either way Henry is the knight-errant he dreamed of being as a boy.

The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 1: Infernal D.outcome: Investigating the cave and dealing with the soldier opens Johanka's questline. The wiki advises leaving later chapters until after The Die is Cast.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 1: Infernal D.tip: Read the Infernal Justice achievement before fighting the soldier; luring him near the shaft so he falls also keeps a Merciful run clean.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 1: Infernal D.immersion: Visit the cave by day, sober and unhurried; Henry knew these hills before Skalitz burned, and the bodies should land hard.

From the Ashes.outcome: Rebuilding Pribyslavitz gives a growing income, a home and recruits from earlier quests. Neglecting wages unsettles villagers and Divish.
From the Ashes.tip: Keep plenty of coin in the village chest. Build woodcutters, then bridge and road, then traders; leave the costly church upgrade until income flows.
From the Ashes.immersion: Return between story beats and walk the village to see progress; recruit people Henry has genuinely helped, like Zach or Matthew and Fritz.

A Place to Call Home.outcome: Unlocks building, recruits and Supplies. Marius's pay terms appear to be cost only; overspending early can strain an unfinished village.
A Place to Call Home.tip: Fund the chest for several days before you leave. Woodcutters' camp costs 2,500 then a daily wage; bridge and road 4,000.
A Place to Call Home.immersion: Henry is a smith's son, not a lord; take Marius's advice seriously and spend carefully rather than pouring loot in at once.

Judgement.outcome: Each ruling shifts reputation, population and income; one judgement per day. Lenient poaching rulings please villagers but may displease Divish.
Judgement.tip: Disputes are random each day; some need specific buildings first. Save before a hearing if you care about a particular result.
Judgement.immersion: Judge as Henry would: fair, a little merciful, and wary of witch accusations. Avoid save-scumming for profit; let verdicts stand.

Supplies.outcome: Contracts for stone, grain, charcoal and livestock; the quest won't close without livestock. Choice of supplier seems to affect only cost.
Supplies.tip: Haggle Rupert's stone to 2,000–3,000 and save first (buggy). Samopesh grain is cheapest; Ledetchko livestock costs 30. Talmberg burners discount charcoal if you saved Ginger.
Supplies.immersion: Ride to each supplier and negotiate in person; pickpocketing Rupert's payment back is out of character for an honest bailiff.

The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 2: Casting Lo.outcome: Cure Ambrose of dice and report back to Guta, who then testifies for Johanka at the Trial. Returning his 600 groschen is the decent close.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 2: Casting Lo.tip: Hustle him: lose two modest games, then stake everything on the third. Win too much early and he quits. Check the You had one job! achievement first.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 2: Casting Lo.immersion: Walk to the market with Johanka in plain clothes and keep your promise to Guta. Henry's here as the preacher's helper, not a card sharp.

The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 3: Go and Sin.outcome: Win Adela over with the healing argument and she becomes a trial witness. Accepting her offer of payment hurts the ending. Killing Henslin costs Ledetchko reputation.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 3: Go and Sin.tip: Get First Aid II and save before talking to her. If Henslin's men ambush you on the road, you can simply outrun them.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 3: Go and Sin.immersion: Turn down Adela's offer at the monastery. Henry is on Johanka's errand, and the refusal fits the penitent arc that's coming.

Next to Godliness.outcome: Beat Archie with fists only, because drawing a weapon fails the quest. Then ask Hans to forgive him, which suits honest Henry better than the pillory. Up to 475 groschen.
Next to Godliness.tip: Take Hans's keys from his trunk in the bathhouse. They open the Rathaus cellar and convince the guard. Failing that check means jail and a failed quest.
Next to Godliness.immersion: Start after 21:00 and walk the dark streets. Klara rejects the bouquet afterwards, so give it to Theresa instead.

Capon's Champion.outcome: Enter under Hans's name. A win earns 100 groschen and golden spurs, and even a loss still pays 100, so there's nothing to lose.
Capon's Champion.tip: Hans covers the 60-groschen entry. Sign up with the Herald and go in fully repaired and fed, because bouts follow one another quickly.
Capon's Champion.immersion: Wait at the lists and treat it as the same morning. You're showing off the 'training' Hans claims he gave his new page.

Clothes Make the Man.outcome: No branches or reward. Hanush scolds Hans and sends you both after Wolflin. Hans's cast-offs are free, and he grumbles if you turn up shabby.
Clothes Make the Man.tip: If you already wear a high-Charisma outfit, Hans skips the offer and his chest never opens. Change first if you want his clothes, and equip them before reporting.
Clothes Make the Man.immersion: Wear the borrowed finery to the audience. A page dressed by his lord is exactly what Hanush should see.

Robber Baron.outcome: Best: parley so Wolflin leaves the loot and pays compensation, pleasing Bernard and Hanush. Letting him keep the loot shames Hanush; a duel becomes an ambush.
Robber Baron.tip: Go unarmed in the Oleshnitz waffenrock. Hear his whole story, then say Hanush knows nothing of Milota's lies. A Bard or Amor potion helps. Give Lumir's wife three bandages.
Robber Baron.immersion: Ride out with Bernard's column and follow the blood trail from the southern farm on foot. Don't hunt for the marker.

Honeyed Words.outcome: Feed Hans the right verses and stall the butcher so his night succeeds. Killing the butcher or Karolina fails it, and the DLC needs it to finish the game.
Honeyed Words.tip: Carry a Marigold decoction for Hans's swollen face. Use lines from the first poem, blame the French, then pass the Speech checks and start singing.
Honeyed Words.immersion: Read the poetry book Hans gives you before meeting him (20:00–21:00), then hide in the churchyard bushes like a proper wingman.

Game of Throws.outcome: Winning the dice tournament gets the whole prize chest and I Can Quit Any Time. Naming Mladota to Anselm earns a hat. Confessing to Erhart gets only the necklace.
Game of Throws.tip: Mladota rolls Alphonse's loaded dice. Pickpocket them in the small hours before you face him. Bring 1,000 groschen unless you can talk your way in free.
Game of Throws.immersion: Wear noble clothes and quiz Anselm about Alphonse first, so your disguise holds when Erhart tests you.

The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 4: Troublemak.outcome: Send the gang off by threatening them with the stocks, no blood needed. Paying (about 100, haggled) to learn who sent them is optional.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 4: Troublemak.tip: Speak to the Loudmouth before you draw steel. The stocks threat settles it quickly, while a brawl risks reputation outside the monastery.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 4: Troublemak.immersion: Invoke the law as Radzig's man rather than starting a street fight near the convent.

The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 5: Bonum Comm.outcome: Hand the treasure over honestly and donate in Pavel's name to the bailiff, overseer or Father Fabian. Lying, self-credit or a failed monastery pitch hurts the trial.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 5: Bonum Comm.tip: Search the roadside corpses for the Custodian's orders. Hand them in with your Cuman report for 325 groschen.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 5: Bonum Comm.immersion: Go at dusk in dark clothes and slip past the Cumans rather than butchering them. That fits Like a Ghost and the spirit of Johanka's work.

No Rest for the Wicked.outcome: Finishing the haunting earns the musk recipe and 675 groschen. If you buy (2,000) or steal the recipe instead, this quest will eventually fail.
No Rest for the Wicked.tip: Stock meat (50 venison, 25 lamb, 4 chickens), 3 charcoal and the fake-blood herbs first. Don't save/load after 'see the Charlatan in the morning', or Felix can bug.
No Rest for the Wicked.immersion: Grave-robbing sits badly with Henry. Make amends by giving Lev's bones a Christian burial in Rattay.

The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 6: The Wicket.outcome: Confess honestly to Johanka, because denials cost her trust. Pray at every shrine and at the Uzhitz church, donate to Godwin and tell him her story.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 6: The Wicket.tip: Pick up the Matthew of Janow manuscript from Godwin's house. Read it before the Trial and return it afterwards.
The Madonna of Sasau — Ch. 6: The Wicket.immersion: Walk the pilgrimage in the penitent's robe instead of riding (about ten in-game hours). It also backs up your 'initiation trial' story for the watching crimps.

If You Can't Beat 'em.outcome: Win the fight-club tournament (Weed, one more, then Punch) for 375 plus the tanner's 300 and the crimps' lead. It also keeps Revenge of the Cuman King open.
If You Can't Beat 'em.tip: The crimps only meet after 22:00. Kneel at the Sasau church altar. Fight all three extra brawlers for more Unarmed experience.
If You Can't Beat 'em.immersion: Turn up at the quarry in the evening as a rough commoner looking for work, not in Radzig's colours. You're auditioning as bandit material.

Poverty, Chastity and Obedience.outcome: Get rid of Manfred without bloodshed, take the writ and purse, and give Karl his whole purse. Killing Manfred loses Karl, and short-changing him sours or starts a fight.
Poverty, Chastity and Obedience.tip: Henry must be able to read. Stash your gear in your own chest before speaking to the porter, because anything handed over can come back marked stolen.
Poverty, Chastity and Obedience.immersion: Report to Radzig first. His wish to take Pious alive should shape how Henry handles the monastery.

A Needle in a Haystack.outcome: Faking Pious's death with blood spares him and still fools the bandits. Arresting him pleases Radzig but loses his strange dice. Killing him inside the walls brings the guards.
A Needle in a Haystack.tip: Never reveal your mission or accuse anyone until the side quests confirm it. A wrong accusation can get you thrown out. Write 'blood' on the kitchen order list.
A Needle in a Haystack.immersion: Wear only the habit and slippers and keep every bell of the timetable. Save sneaking for the night hours. Shave beforehand for the pre-rendered scenes.

In the Cloister.outcome: No lasting effect. Either feed Nevlas dirt for the abbot election or report his forbidden-book scheme to Brother John. Stay friendly with everyone until Pious is found.
In the Cloister.tip: The Cockerel recipe and herbs are given to you, so brew several for long nights. Spare potions from the bench buy lockpicks from Cellarius.
In the Cloister.immersion: Read Everyday Labours and obey the bells: 4th-hour mass, meals, fratery, scriptorium, bed. Sneak about only while the Circators are drinking.

Libri Prohibiti.outcome: Delivering the book wins Nevlas's gratitude and opens The Abbot's List. Reporting him fails the quest and makes him furious.
Libri Prohibiti.tip: Finish Scattered Pages first and the librarian hands you the cabinet key. If you took Avicenna during Restless Spirit, you'll have to sneak out to fetch it.
Libri Prohibiti.immersion: Henry tells himself it's medicine for a dying abbot. Take the book at night, after the copyist has left the library.

Scattered Pages.outcome: Returning all ten pages wins the librarian's trust and the key to the forbidden-books cabinet, which makes Libri Prohibiti trivial.
Scattered Pages.tip: Four pages sit in locked chests or cabinets and one is in the Abbot's bedroom. Collect that one while doing The Abbot's List.
Scattered Pages.immersion: Pick pages up as you go about your chores rather than ransacking the cloister in one go.

Nasty Habits.outcome: Bringing the Custodian's cask makes the Circators friendly, and that covers you on later night prowls. Reporting them to the Prior fails the quest.
Nasty Habits.tip: There's a spare key on a shelf in the far kitchen storeroom, so you can skip Cellarius's 200 groschen. Wait at the door for Jodok and be back before sunrise.
Nasty Habits.immersion: Sit and drink when the Circators invite you. Refusing would blow Brother Gregor's cover.

The Abbot's List.outcome: The records clear up several novices' stories and narrow down who Pious could be. It's key evidence before your Pious decision.
The Abbot's List.tip: Use the Prior's keys or pick the locks during the Circators' cellar hours. Grab the torn page by the Abbot's bed while you're there.
The Abbot's List.immersion: Read in place and leave everything as you found it. Brother Gregor was never here.

Worldly Goods.outcome: The stash is Siskin's escape money, his father's dagger and a book, which rules him out as Pious. Handing it to the Circators or Prior only punishes a harmless lad.
Worldly Goods.tip: After morning mass, follow Siskin to the north dormitory room and catch him at the paver. Speaking to him first completes it on discovery.
Worldly Goods.immersion: Henry steals only for the mission. Leave the novice his savings and keep his secret.

The Trials of a Novice.outcome: Talk a Circator round with a Speech check. Lucas then trusts you and shares what he knows about Pious. Going to the Prior instead fails Nasty Habits.
The Trials of a Novice.tip: Finish Nasty Habits first. Friendly Circators are much easier to persuade.
The Trials of a Novice.immersion: Henry has no love for bullies. Settle it quietly, brother to brother, rather than causing a scandal.

The Madonna of Sasau — The Trial.outcome: Do every preparation step, call every witness and challenge every charge. The best verdict frees Johanka, and Sebastian then gives you his vom Berg sword.
The Madonna of Sasau — The Trial.tip: Steal the Inquisitor's retinue papers to get past the jail guard. Take Matthias's lucky dice to Johanka. Never try to bribe Hashek.
The Madonna of Sasau — The Trial.immersion: Return the Janow manuscript to Father Godwin afterwards, a good penitent's last act.

The Die is Cast.outcome: Story-driven point of no return. Bring Pious's dice (or 3,000 groschen). Keeping your bargain with Zbyshek honours your word, while denouncing him gets him hanged.
The Die is Cast.tip: Free lockpicks are in the shack left of the barn door, and Erik's trunk key is under the small barrel by his desk. Clear any guard in the office first.
The Die is Cast.immersion: Finish side quests before you go, and leave your horse and dog behind. Henry walks in alone as a recruit.

Payback.outcome: Story battle, no choices. You must reach Talmberg by 15:00 or it's game over.
Payback.tip: If your gear is still at Vranik, ask Bernard for the Pirkstein armoury chest. Take a polearm from the first inner-wall wave. It stays equipped for the next quest.
Payback.immersion: Ride straight to Talmberg with the army. No detours or errands while the lords wait.

Out of the Frying Pan.outcome: Story-driven, no choices. The ending plays the same whatever you do.
Out of the Frying Pan.tip: Killing every bandit in the outer bailey completes the quest even if you never touch the portcullis winch.

Night Raid.outcome: Scripted. Whatever you say to Hans, the raid ends the same way. Getting spotted early just turns it into a straight escape.
Night Raid.tip: Change into dark, quiet gear before talking to Robard. Take down the stairs guard first; follow Hans through the shadows.
Night Raid.immersion: Follow Hans's route through the shadows and kill only the two gate guards you were sent for.

Siege.outcome: Finish every optional task (meat, beer, priest, physician, Cockerel potions) to buff your allies in the coming battles and earn Talmberger.
Siege.tip: Andrew at the Inn in the Glade is the only beer source. Herbalists brew only at high reputation, so otherwise brew 60 yourself. Nicodemus comes readily after In God's Hands.
Siege.immersion: Play the camp's errand-runner on horseback. Visiting each supplier in person makes the siege feel lived-in.

Rocketeer.outcome: Forge the commission, return the original and stop Peychar before Konrad leaves: 1,075 groschen and Feyfar's trunk key. Punching Konrad costs goodwill; freeing Peychar invites attack.
Rocketeer.tip: Konrad's 'password' is a joke, and the scribe needs an hour. Peychar starts picking the lock at about 00:45.
Rocketeer.immersion: Keep the midnight watch in the monastery garden yourself, in dark clothes, rather than skipping time.

Revenge of the Cuman King.outcome: Beat Lam, Asch and the King, then all four together when Odd Bird refuses to pay. Fists only. A death breaks the quest and the money is lost.
Revenge of the Cuman King.tip: Strip each beaten fighter's armour between rounds and loot the books. If Odd Bird won't start the next bout, reload and decline his first offer.
Revenge of the Cuman King.immersion: Fighting in Skalitz's old sheep pen makes it a fitting homecoming. Come sober and armoured.

Cold Steel, Hot Blood.outcome: Story battle, no choices. The ford holds whatever you do.
Cold Steel, Hot Blood.tip: Havel's men go for the Skalitz militia before you. Flank them or shoot them from behind.
Cold Steel, Hot Blood.immersion: Stay with the Skalitz men you're leading instead of charging ahead alone.

Family Values.outcome: Story-driven. Passing all four persuasion checks earns the Freud achievement; the story beats stay the same.
Family Values.tip: Erik's persuasion stats are high. Wear your best clean armour for the Charisma and Badassness checks.

An Oath is an Oath.outcome: Story-driven, no choices. The finale plays out after the storming.
An Oath is an Oath.tip: The two-day bombardment is free time for errands such as the encampment scouting. Make a hard save before you tell Robard you're ready to attack.
An Oath is an Oath.immersion: Ride beside Hans to Skalitz rather than fast-travelling. It's Henry's road home.

Epilogue.outcome: The game ends when you speak to Sir Hans at the camp. You can free-roam until then.
Epilogue.tip: Meet Jobst in daylight. Drink a Saviour Schnapps before the final talk with Hans so you can come back to free roam.
Epilogue.immersion: Use the 'couple of days' to say farewells in Rattay and Skalitz before riding out.
